rationale: rule:prospecting_default

Near-term intent is clear (packaging project in eight weeks, wants commercial info this week) and the drawing permits several optical technologies so fit is not the blocker, but spend level and the component purchase signer are unknown.

There is near-term intent (packaging project starting in eight weeks, documented counting-error pain) but the controls engineer cannot state a budget or name who releases component purchases, and the founder has dropped out of the conversation; the drawing already permits several optical technologies, so fit is not the blocker.
rule:technical_review_with_incumbent

The only open issue is whether the sensor's wetted materials tolerate the new cleaning liquid, and the engineer can supply composition, concentration and temperature in writing, so a documented compatibility/spec review is the next step; budget, contact, price and delivery are already settled.

Chemical compatibility of the wetted parts with the new cleaning liquid is unconfirmed, and per the PT/PC records such resistance must be checked per application from the customer's written medium, concentration and temperature data, which the engineer can supply; budget and purchasing contact already exist, so spec fit is the open item.
rule:trust_concern_with_incumbent_late

Specs (interface, resolution, mounting) and price/delivery are already signed off, an unreliable incumbent gives a switch motive, and the only remaining concern is unproven performance during winding cycles plus unwillingness to convert all encoders at once 
combined with one machine available for a limited trial.

Interface, resolution and mounting specs are signed off with price and delivery agreed, budget authority exists for a limited quantity, and the only remaining doubt is product performance during real winding cycles plus unwillingness to switch all encoders at once — a single-machine trial addresses exactly that switching risk.
rule:trust_concern

Budget is set and the published range fits the application, so the only open barrier is her doubt about our experience serving ceramic equipment manufacturers; credibility must be established before any trial, and she has not made equipment available for evaluation.

Budget is set and the published range already suits the application, so the only open issue is the owner's doubt that we have served ceramic equipment makers and understand their service expectations — a supplier-trust concern, not a product-performance one, and she has not offered equipment for a trial.
rule:supplier_audit_required

Specs, pricing and budget are all settled; the only remaining barrier is the customer's supplier admission procedure, which mandates an in-person audit of calibration and traceability at our premises since document review is explicitly insufficient, and the quality manager has availability nearby next month.

Specs are accepted, budget approved and pricing/delivery agreed; the only remaining barrier is the customer's supplier admission procedure requiring an in-person audit of calibration and traceability at our premises, which documents cannot replace.
rule:price_objection_late_stage

Validation is complete and the owner (sole decision maker) accepts delivery, warranty and payment terms, leaving a firm 12% discount demand on a 2,400-unit annual commitment as the only barrier; she rejected lot-splitting alternatives, so the discount must be approved above the seller's authority.

Validation is complete and all other terms (delivery, warranty, payment) are accepted by the owner, who is the decision maker with near-term timing; the only barrier is a requested 12 percent discount, far above the 5 percent sales authority, so the sales director must approve.
rule:prospecting_default

Technical fit is confirmed and the customer keeps our catalogue for the planned redesign, but purchasing and engineering both state no component purchases or supplier change before the redesign in eighteen months — a future opportunity rather than a hard mismatch.

Fit is confirmed (housing and electrical interface match) but both engineering and purchasing state no purchase or supplier change until the redesign in eighteen months, which matches the 12-24 month design cycle; the opportunity is real but not near-term.
rule:qualifying_default

A one-off need for four units with a confirmed zero follow-on volume cannot support a custom housing development, and no standard catalogue housing fits the fixed mounting space, so the mismatch is structural rather than timing-related.

A custom housing is required (no standard DS housing fits the fixed mounting space), but the need is four units total with no repeat demand, far below the non-negotiable 300-unit minimum for custom variants; time will not change this.
rule:budget_or_authority_unclear

Near-term intent is clear (replacement needed within six weeks, no contractual block, price in line, specs self-checked as matching), but funding and authority are unresolved: finance claims a frozen equipment budget, the engineer cannot confirm the maintenance account balance or who releases it, and the signing purchasing manager has not responded.

Specs appear to match and there is near-term intent (replacement needed in six weeks) plus a switching motive, but it is unresolved which budget applies, what its balance is and who can release it, and the purchasing manager who signs orders has not responded.
rule:prospecting_default

Budget, decision team and timing are already established, but product fit for polished, curved, moving targets is unconfirmed and engineering refuses to accept catalogue repeatability figures; the customer can supply reflectivity data, drawings, speed profiles and tolerances electronically, so a document-based specification review is the right next step rather than an on-site assessment.

Budget, decision team and timing are already established, but the LD series repeatability is only specified for flat matte stationary targets, while the application involves polished, curved, moving workpieces — so product fit is still open and engineering refuses to accept catalogue figures. The customer can supply reflectivity data, drawings, speed profiles and tolerances electronically, so a document-based specification review is sufficient.
rule:trust_concern_with_incumbent_late

Specs, commercial terms, budget and supplier qualification are all settled, and the only open issue is unproven sustained performance on dusty produce in their own process \u2014 with an idle spare lane and purchasing able to authorize a small quantity, a trial order directly addresses the product-performance risk before harvest.

Specs are signed off, supplier qualification is complete, budget and terms are agreed, and the only open concern is proven sustained performance on dusty produce in the customer's own process — with an idle sorting lane and purchasing able to release a small quantity, a pilot on one line addresses the switching risk.
rule:trust_concern

Budget, roles and timing are already settled and the specs look suitable, but management doubts our credibility in laundry machinery and explicitly asks for a comparable reference before committing evaluation resources, so trust must be established before any trial.

Budget, roles and timing are settled and the specs are considered suitable, but management doubts our experience in laundry machinery and explicitly blocks any evaluation resources until comparable references are shown, so trust must be established before a trial.
rule:technical_review_with_incumbent

Specs (interface and measurement range) already match, but the usable mounting clearance and cable route behind a moving guard cannot be determined from drawings or photos and must be measured on the running machine, with an escorted maintenance window opening in three weeks.

Specs (interface and range) already match and budget/decision maker are in place; the only open item is mounting clearance and cable routing behind a moving guard, which cannot be established from drawings or photos and must be measured on site during the maintenance window in three weeks.
rule:price_objection_late_stage

Specs are accepted, quality has approved the supplier, terms and schedule are agreed, and the confirmed decision maker states price is the only remaining barrier — a 14% reduction that exceeds typical seller discount authority, with a deadline one week before the month-end board award.

Technical acceptance, supplier approval and delivery/payment terms are all complete, leaving the required 14 percent reduction as the sole barrier; that far exceeds the 5 percent sales authority and must go to the sales director, with the board deadline making timing critical.
rule:no_near_term_plan

Fit is confirmed (enclosure dimensions and interface match) but an exclusive incumbent agreement runs for eleven more months and both managers have stated in writing that no transaction will occur until then, with the next design generation starting ~2 months after expiry.

Fit is confirmed (dimensions and interface match) but an exclusive agreement runs for eleven more months with no transaction permitted, and detailed design for the next generation starts about two months after it ends, so the opportunity is real but future-dated.
rule:technical_review_default

The frozen, non-negotiable specification demands continuous 420 degrees Celsius operation in a sealed space with no option for remote mounting, cooling or a protective sleeve, so the thermal requirement exceeds what any sensor head we could offer would survive and no mitigation path remains; volume, funding and timing cannot resolve a physical specification mismatch.

The frozen specification requires continuous 420 °C sensor head operation with no remote mounting or sleeve possible, while the TS series tops out at 180 °C with no higher-temperature version existing or planned — a hard specification mismatch that time will not resolve.
rule:proposal_default

Specs are technically accepted and delivery timing works with production needed in ten weeks, but it is unknown whether the integrator's purchasing or the manufacturer's central team will issue the order and no spending allocation is confirmed, while the approving engineer has no purchasing authority.

The design is technically accepted and production is needed in ten weeks, but it is unresolved whether the integrator's purchasing office or the manufacturer's central team will issue the order, no spending allocation is confirmed, and the approving engineer has no purchasing authority.
rule:qualifying_default

Budget, authority and timing are already confirmed and the indicative price accepted, but the product fit is open because startup pressure peaks and repeated overload duration are missing; the customer can send logs and drawings electronically, so a document-based spec review suffices rather than a site visit.

Budget, authority and timing are confirmed and price is accepted, but the product fit is still open because startup pressure peaks and repeated overload duration are unknown relative to the 1.5x overload limit; the customer can send logs and drawings electronically, so a document review suffices.
rule:negotiation_default

Price, delivery and specifications are already agreed and the incumbent is discontinuing the housing, so the only remaining barrier is operators' fear of unexpected stops over a full shift — a product performance concern that a limited run on the available isolated line, for which procurement has authority and funds, can resolve.

Specs, price and terms are agreed and the incumbent is discontinuing the housing, but the remaining concern is product performance over a full shift; procurement has funds and an isolated line for a limited initial quantity, which matches a staged trial on one line.
rule:technical_review_default

Specs and funding are already accepted, but the operations director doubts our credibility outside laboratory equipment and has blocked machine time — an industry-experience trust gap must be closed before any trial or on-site work.

Specs are accepted and funding confirmed, but the operations director doubts our experience outside laboratory equipment and has blocked machine time, so credibility in paper converting production and maintenance support must be established before any trial or on-site work.
rule:supplier_audit_required

Specs and measurement range are already accepted and budget is approved, so the only gate is the customer's mandatory on-site supplier qualification audit witnessing calibration and assembly identification, which explicitly cannot be replaced by documents, photos or a video call.

Specs and budget are already accepted; the only barrier is the customer's mandatory supplier qualification audit, which its quality policy requires to be witnessed in person at our premises, so documents or a video call will not suffice.
rule:price_objection_late_stage

All technical, approval, payment and delivery items are settled with funded annual volume of 6,000 units; the only remaining barrier is an explicit 8% price gap (92 vs 100) that the buyer refuses to trade against service or shipping concessions, so approval beyond the seller's discount authority is needed.

Technical acceptance, supplier approval, payment and delivery terms are all closed, leaving price as the only barrier; the requested 8 percent discount (92 vs 100) exceeds the 5 percent sales authority and the buyer has ruled out trading service or shipping terms.
rule:technical_review_default

Product fit is confirmed and we are an approved supplier with drawings retained, but the board postponed the machine platform to the next financial year with no component purchases for at least nine months, so there is no near-term buying opportunity yet a clear future one.

Technical fit is confirmed and we are an approved supplier, but the machine platform is postponed with no component purchases for at least nine months; engineering retains the approved drawings for restart, so the opportunity is future, not lost.
rule:prospecting_default

The signed engineering requirement permits only the controller vendor's proprietary communication protocol with no converters and a contractually locked interface, so any standard-interface sensor is a fundamental specification mismatch that time and budget cannot resolve.

The customer's signed requirement permits only the controller vendor's proprietary protocol and forbids converters, while the LP absolute linear series supports only SSI, IO-Link and analog, with no gateways or customer-specific firmware available — a hard specification mismatch time cannot resolve.
rule:negotiation_default

Specs and price are already accepted, so the only open issue is authority and budget: the purchasing contact claims verbal owner approval and a spare-parts exemption, while the owner states capital spending is suspended and no approval record exists, yet an order is claimed for next month.

Technical fit and price are already accepted, so the only open issue is money: the owner states capital spending is suspended while the purchasing contact claims a spare-parts classification and next-month approval without any approval record. Budget classification and authority rest with the owner/finance, so that must be confirmed before proceeding.
rule:proposal_default

Commercial terms (funding, authority, price, delivery) are settled, but the fluid viscosity requirement is contradictory (50 vs 12,000 mPa·s) and the engineer can supply fluid and temperature records today, so product fit must be confirmed before proceeding.

The FL series only works up to 2,000 mPa·s, and the file contains conflicting viscosity figures (50 vs 12,000 mPa·s) with the engineer offering to send the fluid and temperature records today, so the specification match is still unconfirmed even though budget, authority, price and delivery are settled.
rule:trust_concern

All dimensions, signal, speed and resolution specs were verified and signed off and pricing is accepted, with the only remaining doubt being counting stability during repeated start/stop cycles; the incumbent's poor availability gives switching motive, and the owner can self-approve a limited quantity with a spare machine available for trial.

Specs are fully signed off and pricing accepted, with an incumbent supply problem driving the switch; the only remaining concern is product behavior (counting stability during repeated starts) and the owner can approve a limited quantity for the spare machine.
rule:proposal_default

Specs, price, delivery and paperwork are all accepted; the sole remaining barrier is the owner's doubt that we have experience in dusty cutting workshops rather than electronics assembly, and he will not commit technician or machine time (so no trial or visit) until that credibility is established.

The customer accepts spec fit, price and delivery but doubts our supplier experience in dusty cutting workshops and will not release technician or machine time until that doubt is resolved, so comparable-application references (cutting reports) must come first.
rule:budget_or_authority_unclear

Specs and price are already accepted, but the large customer's quality rule mandates an on-site audit of our production line and serial-number traceability before supplier approval, and certificates cannot waive it.

Specs and price are accepted and funding is available; the only remaining barrier is the customer's mandatory supplier-approval audit of our production line and serial-number traceability, which certificates cannot waive.
rule:price_objection_late_stage

Technical acceptance, approval, and terms are all settled with no incumbent; the sole remaining barrier is an explicit nine percent price reduction driven by a fixed component allowance that no spec, consolidation or volume change can offset, so it needs pricing authority above the seller.

Technical acceptance, approval and commercial terms are all settled, leaving price as the only barrier, and the required nine percent discount exceeds the 5 percent sales authority; the customer has already ruled out volume, spec and shipment trade-offs.
rule:negotiation_default

Technical and commercial terms are already agreed and our product remains on the approved list, but the customer's machine programme is postponed twelve months with the purchase date withdrawn and no interim component or stock need, so there is a real future opportunity rather than a hard mismatch.

Terms and technical approval are agreed and our product stays on the approved supplier list, but the owner and purchasing have jointly withdrawn the purchase date for twelve months and need nothing in the interim, so the opportunity is real but not near-term.
rule:technical_review_with_incumbent

The customer has a finalized, hard technical requirement (true absolute position after power loss, no homing, no battery-backed counter) and the product's fit against that spec has not yet been confirmed, so a spec review is the gating step before any trial or commercial motion.

The finalized, unchangeable design requires absolute position after power loss without homing and without battery-backed counters, while the RE series is incremental only with no absolute version or position-retaining accessory planned  a hard requirement that cannot be met regardless of budget or timing.
rule:budget_or_authority_unclear

Technical acceptance is complete with near-term need (parts in seven weeks) and pricing aligned, but neither division owns the component budget, no signing purchasing manager is identified, and finance has received no funding request.

Technical acceptance is complete and parts are needed in seven weeks (near-term intent), but neither division owns the component budget, no purchasing signer is identified, and finance has no funding request.
rule:price_objection_late_stage

The engineer introduced a hotter cleaning cycle that conflicts with the accepted specification and no one has confirmed which revision governs, so temperature fit is unresolved; the cycle record can be sent electronically, making a document review sufficient before addressing the 10 percent price request.

A new hotter cleaning cycle was added outside the accepted specification and nobody has confirmed which revision governs, so technical fit is unresolved and price is not the only remaining barrier; the engineer can send the cycle record electronically, so a document review suffices rather than a site visit.
rule:trust_concern_with_incumbent_late

Specifications and proposal terms are accepted, the incumbent's delays give a switch motive, and the clarified objection is detection consistency in dusty shifts on the customer's own line — a product performance risk — while funds, a separate production cell and authority for a limited quantity exist and management requires operating evidence before full changeover.

Specifications and terms are already accepted, an incumbent exists with delayed parts as switch motive, and the 'unproven' doubt resolves to product performance evidence on the customer's own dusty line rather than supplier credibility; funds, a separate cell and authority for a limited quantity are in place.
rule:trust_concern_with_incumbent_late

Specs, price and delivery are accepted, so the only remaining barrier is management's doubt about our track record with battery machinery customers — and the operations director will not release machine time or funds for a trial until that credibility question is answered, so reference evidence must precede any pilot.

Specs, price and delivery are accepted, but management doubts our track record with comparable battery machinery businesses and will not release machine time or funds for product evaluation until that is answered, so supplier credibility must be established before any trial.
rule:negotiation_default

All commercial and technical terms are settled; the only remaining barrier is that the quality head, who signs supplier admissions, requires an on-site witnessing of calibration handling, so document review is explicitly insufficient.

Specs, budget and price are settled; the only remaining barrier is that the quality head, who signs supplier admissions, requires witnessing calibration handling at our premises, which uploaded certificates cannot replace.
rule:qualifying_default

Engineering and quality approvals are already complete, volume (22,000 units/yr) and commercial terms are accepted, and the buyer has award authority, so the only open barrier is the required 13% reduction, which exceeds normal seller discount authority.

Technical and quality approvals are done, warranty/payment/delivery are accepted, and the buyer has award authority, so price is the only remaining barrier; the required 13 percent reduction far exceeds the 5 percent sales authority and needs sales director approval with target price and the 22,000 unit annual volume.
rule:prospecting_default

The programme director and purchasing head confirmed this week that the feature is deferred fifteen months with no parts or evaluation spend authorized, while our published spec fits the application — a good fit with no near-term purchase plan, so the engineer's stale 'urgent' thread should not drive action.

Authoritative stakeholders (programme director and purchasing head) confirmed the feature is deferred 15 months with no parts or evaluation spend authorized, so there is no near-term purchase despite good spec fit and an engineer's stale 'urgent' emails; the machine-builder design cycle means the order comes when detailed design starts.
rule:hard_requirement_unmet

The buyer has a concrete, non-negotiable requirement (independent hygienic certification for wetted sensor assemblies) plus budget and ~600 units/year, but nothing in the scenario confirms whether our sensor holds that certification, so specification fit must be verified before any trial or disqualification.

The end customer's signed spec requires independent third-party hygienic certification for wetted sensor assemblies and will not accept a manufacturer's declaration, while the LV series has no such certification and the company has no programme to obtain one — a hard requirement that time will not resolve.
